doc.title: Jamey Aebersold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 26, 2022

title: Never meeting anyone who can't improvise
summary: Tone-deaf workshop attendee story, then a stop-smoking book given to a smoker.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Have you ever run across someone that you had multiple encounters with in teaching and you decided well I found someone who can’t improvise?

There’s a couple of kids in this class that are just struggling, but I don’t even think we’ve gotten to the point of improvising. I’m just trying to get them to [takes deep breath] take a good breath, support their tone and play the scale. I don’t think they’re scared to death, they’re just fumbling to play the instrument. But everybody else, no I’ve never found anybody that can’t improvise. I do remember one person years ago, I was doing my two- day workshop and this guy comes up to me on a break, I’m setting up the piano. And he said, “Mr. Aebersold, I’m tone deaf.” I said, “Oh you are?” “He said, “Yeah, I’m tone deaf.” I said, “Well let’s see.” So I hit a note and he doesn’t hit that note. He sings something else. I hit another note, he doesn’t sing that note. I said, “Okay, here we go. I’m going to hit the note, and you think about it. Don’t open your mouth until you think you’ve got that note.” So I hit another note. Just keep thinking. I hit the note, just keep thinking. And finally he very faintly goes, “Laaaaa.” And it happened to be the note. And I hit it again and I said, “Are you sure?” “Laaaaa. I think so.” “What is that? I don’t know if you’re listening.” “Laaaaa.” I said, “Guess what?” He said, “What?” I said, “You’re not tone deaf you’re just not thinking. And then we played other notes, we played other notes and he got them. I said, “So you can’t say that anymore. Forget that. You’re not tone deaf.” So sometimes it’s a quick thing like that that I hope changes somebody. That’s like — I know you want to close here but I’m down to the post office today and I come outside, here’s a fellow leaning over talking to two people in the car and he’s smoking. And boy can I smell the smoke and I hate smoking. And then he leans back about six feet and kind of leans against the pole. I walked past him and I could smell the smoke all along here. So I go and get a — I don’t have one in front of me here, a quit easy stop smoking book that I published. I printed 50,000 of them and I’m giving them out. Okay? I have one in my van. So I went over and got it, I walked back up and he looks at me and I said, “I’ve heard your cough before and I’ve smelled that smell before.
